q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of corn flakes per kg?
title: Corn flakes carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the maize grits, sugar and malt per kg with supplier figures. Then add cooking, flaking and toasting energy, a large plant energy use, plus packing, and divide the plant's energy by kg of flakes packed.

ul: Drying, flaking rolls and toasting ovens.

p: Report per kg by product. Cartons are a real share for cereals, so list them separately.

example.title: Worked example: corn flakes unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 59,150 / 200,000 = 0.296 kg CO2 per kg
Add grits, sugar and cartons for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
